episode_title: The end of SaaS: Why AI will replace your software, with Ingo Paas | Builders

real_qa.q: Why will SaaS applications disappear when AI is properly implemented in organizations?
real_qa.r: When AI comes and processes are automated correctly, SaaS applications become unnecessary because the process itself disappears. Humans would only need to do observational work to control whether decisions made by the system align with business model, strategies and goals. The objective should be to get rid of these applications and replace SaaS with AI instead of using AI to solve problems between fragmented applications.

real_qa.q: What does effective AI governance look like when traditional linear governance models fail?
real_qa.r: Effective AI governance must be operational and embedded into the core of your business. You need to control what is happening with AI in real-time to ensure any decision is done on behalf of your business rather than what the AI system thinks is right. Similar to how cybersecurity systems monitor enterprise infrastructure in real-time with Red and Blue Sox services, you need AI capability that monitors and translates AI activities into something humans understand, rather than relying on traditional linear governance processes.

real_qa.q: Where are AI systems already making autonomous decisions at scale today?
real_qa.r: Surveillance systems are purely AI-based, working in real-time and making autonomous decisions. They are implemented by authorities, states and governments. Military warfare systems represent another example where decision authority is moving to the moment the technology makes life-or-death decisions. These demonstrate AI at full-scale implementation where two AI capabilities (surveillance and warfare) are coming together, which represents the complexity enterprises need to prepare for.
real_qa.requete: AI autonomous decision making surveillance warfare

real_qa.q: How should organizations balance between maintaining current operations and exploring AI transformation?
real_qa.r: Organizations need balance between exploration and contingency in running their business. You must have people who continue running the business and implementing new SaaS applications until you are ready to replace them, while also having dedicated people building for the future and asking critical questions early enough to avoid certain investments and apply AI instead. This allows you to play with use cases while maintaining portfolio decisions on which problems could be replaced by AI.
real_qa.requete: AI experimentation exploration versus operational continuity

real_qa.q: What prevents boards from having meaningful discussions about AI's impact on organizational decision-making?
real_qa.r: Boards operate in a linear, risk-averse mindset focused on protecting the next quarter, budget and strategy, ensuring compliance and managing governance requirements from the European Union. They rarely ask relevant technology questions and lack understanding of how AI transforms decision authority within organizations. Board certification trains members in frameworks from 20 years ago, all relevant but insufficient for the exponential change AI represents, leaving no time for deeper discussions about how autonomous systems shift decision-making from humans to machines.
real_qa.requete: board discussion AI decision authority governance

real_qa.q: What is the core organizational problem preventing successful AI transformation in enterprises?
real_qa.r: Enterprises are fragmented in their systems, data, integrations, and customer relationships. Current efforts focus on building improvements into existing processes, applications and systems rather than transforming from the core. When AI is added to this fragmented foundation, companies continue doing fragmented work instead of redesigning the organization around intelligent systems. This fragmentation persists despite having built great leaders and governance structures, preventing the fundamental organizational redesign that AI transformation actually requires.

guest.bio_context: Ingo Paas is originally from Germany and has worked with major corporations including Ericsson, Adidas, and ICA in Stockholm. He spent nearly seven years as CIO and CDO at Green Cargo, a state-owned company focused on railroad production and data transformation. He is the author of several books including The Rise of Human Agency and A Billion Times Smarter: Empowering Human Autonomy and Digital Composable Enterprises, and was recently appointed by the Swedish state as a board member at Svenska Kraftnät, which manages regional energy production and delivery for Sweden and the Nordic context.
